newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to host int'l coffee seminar January 20-22.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to host int'l coffee seminar January 20-22.

text.p: Brazil is to host its first international coffee seminar for nine years on January 20-22 in Rio de Janeiro, according to the conference organiser.
The seminar will present the legal framework for future policy to be decided by a new council, expected to be created in the next month, said Francisco Ourique of Flavour Coffee.

Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles, his key coffee official Mauricio Assis and members of the private sector within the new CDPC council will outline the council's 1997/98 program on January 20.
On January 21, the chief economist at the National Coffee Department Jorge Labato will present the new program for regular crop forecasting in Brazil.
Also Leon Yallouz, former USDA representative responsible for the department's Brazilian crop surveys, has been invited to give a speech on his projections for 1997/98 production.
On the same day, the Brazilian roasters' association ABIC will present a report on 1996 consumption in Brazil which provisional data shows could reach 11.5 to 12 million bags.
ABIC will also present its new marketing program which aims to boost internal consumption to 15 million bags in 1997.

On January 22, the managing director of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation Jorge Cardenas and the secretary general of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries Roberio Oliveira will speak on coffee price perspectives and models of price stabilisation.
They wil be joined by Octavio Rainho, former president of the now-defunct Brazilian Coffee Institute and Paulo Haddad, former Brazilian Finance minister.
After the seminar a five-day trip to the south of Minas Gerais and the Cerrado region is being organised for those to wish to visit the country's key production regions, Ourique said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
